consensus_summary: All four blind responses converge on a christological primary meaning: Jesus Christ as the rejected stone made the cornerstone/foundation (Ps 118:22; Isa 28:16; Matt 21:42; Acts 4:11; Eph 2:20; 1 Pet 2:4-8), with the Daniel 2 stone read messianically as Christ/God's kingdom, and believers as 'living stones' built into a spiritual house as the leading secondary sense. Other acknowledged sub-motifs include God as Rock, heart of stone, stone tablets of the Law, memorial stones, and the white stone.
book_summary: The book defines Stone as a person functioning as a building member of a house or kingdom: Jesus is the rejected living Stone made chief cornerstone; believers are living stones built under and aligned to Him; and the Daniel 2 stone cut without hands is Christ as Head of the kingdom that grows into the mountain filling the earth.
consensus_core_identification: Christ as the rejected stone become the cornerstone (with believers as living stones and the Daniel 2 kingdom-stone as standard companion readings).
book_core_identification: A person as a building member of God's house/kingdom — chiefly Christ as the rejected cornerstone, with His people as living stones and the Daniel 2 stone as Christ heading the growing kingdom.
boundary_disagreement: None of substance. The book packages the primary christological reading and the 'living stones' alternative under one generalized rubric ('a person as a building member'), but this is exactly the combined content of the consensus's primary meaning plus its most common alternative; no cases are added or excluded. The book does not mention peripheral sub-motifs (heart of stone, tablets of the Law, memorial stones, white stone), but omission of secondary motifs in a glossary entry is not a boundary dispute.
material_contradiction: None. The book's identifications (Christ as rejected cornerstone, believers as living stones, Daniel's stone as Christ/kingdom) are precisely the consensus readings.
rationale: The consensus core is Christ as the rejected-stone-made-cornerstone, with believers as living stones and the Daniel 2 stone as messianic kingdom readings. The book affirms all three explicitly and even cites the same catena of texts (Isa 28:16; Ps 118:22; Dan 2; Matt 21:42; Eph 2:20-22; 1 Pet 2:4-7). Its umbrella phrasing 'a person as a building member of a house or kingdom' is a formal generalization that unifies the christological and ecclesial senses rather than replacing or reshaping either; the referents and cases covered are the same. The book's slight emphasis that the Daniel stone is 'Christ as Head of the kingdom' aligns with the christological/messianic reading responses A and D already list as standard.
strongest_objection: One could argue the book's abstraction 'a person as a building member' subtly shifts the symbol's center from Christ specifically to a generic architectural-person metaphor, and that treating the Daniel stone as Christ personally (rather than the kingdom) picks a side within a mildly contested reading — which might warrant REFINED. But the book immediately identifies Christ as the chief instance, and Christ-as-Daniel's-stone is an acknowledged consensus option, so the differences remain immaterial wording and framing.
